data.title: Why China is unwilling to be the world's next climate leader
data.description:
Key points:
  • China has decided against hosting the 2028 COP, sources say
  • Little appetite in Beijing to champion global climate diplomacy
  • Delegation at COP has played its traditional low-profile role

By Lewis Jackson

President Xi Jinping showcased China's diplomatic heft this week at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum.

But 5,000 miles away at the COP31 international climate conference in the Turkish city of Antalya, Beijing is sending a different message: we're not the leaders you're looking for.

The exit of the United States from international climate diplomacy under President Donald Trump since last year has left a superpower-sized hole in the COP process that many had hoped China would fill, especially after reports last year it was considering hosting COP33 in 2028.

But Beijing has decided against hosting the annual UN climate conference, two people familiar with the matter said this week. Meanwhile China's envoys to COP31 stuck to the country's accustomed low-key playbook, diplomats and observers to the talks said.

"Yes, we would like to see China take more of a role, simply because right now China is the defender of the international world order and the rule of law in the absence of the previous defenders," said Ralph Regenvanu, Vanuatu's climate minister.

China's delegation has been mostly absent from public events at the two-week conference on Turkey's Mediterranean coast, which is attempting to address rising temperatures and the worsening impacts of climate change.

CHINA SIDES WITH THE DEVELOPING WORLD

Inside the closed-door negotiations, China's delegation fulfilled its traditional role of siding with the developing world's demands that wealthy nations give more climate finance and cut emissions faster, while resisting specific targets for phasing out fossil fuels, diplomats said.

While historically, the Western world has emitted the most greenhouse gases, China is now by far the planet's biggest emitter.

It is also a major part of the solution as the largest producer and exporter of the solar panels, wind turbines and electric vehicles needed to curb carbon emissions.

A Reuters analysis published ahead of the COP31 conference showed that China sent $132 billion in clean technology and investment to the developing world last year, almost on par with all developed world climate finance.

ANOTHER KIND OF LEADERSHIP

The reluctance to leverage those green credentials into a bigger role in international climate diplomacy reflects the prevailing view in Beijing that doing so would have unwelcome consequences, say observers and analysts.

For one, hosting a COP, short for Conference of the Parties, would create pressure for China to propose more ambitious climate targets, which is opposed by groups tied to the country's huge coal sector.

A bigger role on the global climate stage could also spur demands for more climate giving and reopen a long-standing debate over whether the world's second-largest economy belongs in the same league as poorer developing countries.

A person familiar with the Chinese government's thinking said the central government saw no advantage in taking on more formal climate leadership.

"The central government thinks we are already leading on renewable technology, why should we have this COP?" the person said.

China's ministry of foreign affairs did not immediately respond to questions from Reuters.

LINKING TRADE TO CLIMATE

There is one area where Beijing has been willing to take a bigger role: trade.

Just as Xi denounced "rampant protectionism" at the APEC summit this week, Chinese negotiators in Antalya pressed for language on the free flow of green trade as a way to promote the clean-technology industries that have become a major source of economic and geopolitical influence.

That could counter what China sees as trade restrictions the West has imposed only in the name of climate policy.

One European diplomat described the issue as China's key ask in talks with the European Union.

The United States has all but blocked imports of Chinese electric cars with tariffs, while the European Union has also raised barriers to Chinese clean technology and implemented rules designed to tax carbon-heavy imports.

At a pre-COP briefing in Beijing, Li Gao, China's delegation head, told reporters the conference needed to address the "new problem" of unilateralism and protectionism, a common indirect criticism from China of US and European trade policy.

data.title: The Container Store Restores Website, Systems Following Cybersecurity Incident
data.description:
By Connor Hart

The Container Store has restored its website and systems following a recent cybersecurity incident.

Upon detecting suspicious activity, The Container Store immediately activated its established cybersecurity protocols and proactively suspended online order-taking, parent company Neighborhood Intelligence said Friday.

All retail locations remained open, serving customers through alternative transaction-processing procedures, it added.

Neighborhood Intelligence expects a minimal impact on revenue for the quarter due to the incident, with any impact on profitability expected to be mitigated by the company's business interruption insurance.

The incident was isolated to The Container Store, which engaged with independent cybersecurity experts to assist with the investigation, containment and restoration efforts.

"Our investigation into this event is ongoing, however we do not believe that this incident impacted the security of any customer financial data because The Container Store does not store or maintain consumer financial or payment information," Neighborhood Intelligence said.

data.title: Nasdaq Set for Fresh Decline as AI Selloff Intensifies — Update
data.description:
By Joe Stonor

Global stocks sold off and Treasurys strengthened as investor confidence in the artificial-intelligence trade showed signs of cracking.

Nasdaq futures dropped 1.7%, extending sharp falls from the last session. S&P 500 futures fell 0.85%, while contracts tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 0.2%. Major U.S. indexes are on track for their worst week since the announcement of President Trump's so-called Liberation Day tariffs upended global trade in April 2025.

Anthropic's record-breaking IPO failed to stem heavy selling across global stocks. Chip makers, tech giants and cloud-computing stocks weakened in U.S. premarket trade after heavy selling across Asian tech names. The memory chip-dominated Kospi closed 5.2% lower, while Japan's Nikkei also fell more than 5%. Taiwan's Taiex sank 6.2%, bringing its weekly loss to 17.5%--its worst week since 1990.

The selling bled to European stocks, too. ASML, the continent's most valuable stock, tumbled by more than 6% as a basket of the continent's tech stocks traded 4% lower. The continent-wide Stoxx 600 was 1.7% lower.

"I think the market seriously underestimated just how much liquidity Anthropic's IPO would require," said NinjaTrader economist Tracy Shuchart in a post on X. "The question isn't whether investors want exposure to AI. It's whether the market has sufficient liquidity to absorb this much supply without forcing liquidation elsewhere."

The gloominess in stock market sentiment comes despite fresh declines for oil. Benchmark Brent crude contracts dropped around 0.3% to $91.70 a barrel. West Texas Intermediate contracts fell 0.7% to trade around $82.60 a barrel. The U.S. Energy Information Administration said Thursday that oil shipments through major Middle Eastern shipping routes increased 19% in the third quarter.

Lower oil prices and an investor flight to safety combined to strengthen Treasurys. Ten-year yields fell back below 5.000%, while two-year yields dropped 8.7 basis points to 4.690%. Thirty-year yields fell 5.3 basis points to trade around 5.340%.

Metals prices continued to sell off, with gold tumbling over 3% to $3,570 a troy ounce. Silver contracts fell close to 5%. The dollar held near multimonth highs, while bitcoin hovered around lows not seen since the beginning of July, trading at $61,530.

For the day ahead, macro watchers will look to Michigan's consumer sentiment index for November, and to Federal Reserve speakers including Christopher Waller.

data.title: Boardwalk REIT Gets TSX Okay to Buy Back Up To 10% of Public Float
data.description:
By Adriano Marchese

Boardwalk Real Estate Investment Trust intends to launch a share-repurchase program to buy back up to 10% of the company's trust units over the next year.

The REIT on Friday said that the Toronto Stock Exchange has approved its normal course issuer bid to buy back up to 3.6 million trust units for cancellation.

Boardwalk's units have been under pressure so far into 2026, falling about 8% since the start of the year to close on Thursday at 59.34 Canadian dollars ($41.38).

At Thursday's closing price, the value of the units intended for buyback would be worth about C$214.4 million.

The company can begin buying back the units starting Nov. 24.

data.title: Danaher, Microsoft Partner on AI Platform for Scientific Instruments
data.description:
By Kelly Cloonan

Danaher and Microsoft are teaming up to develop an agentic AI platform designed for scientific instruments and laboratories.

Danaher said Friday the partnership aims to help streamline experimental operations and speed up laboratory findings.

The platform will be built on Microsoft's AI technologies using Danaher's scientific, workflow and instrumentation expertise. It will aim to enable reuse and interoperability across technologies, so specialized products can be built on a shared foundation while remaining open to agents and digital solutions in multi-vendor laboratories, Danaher said.

Danaher said that while the platform is still under development, its first commercial AI applications--including an AI assistant designed to provide product support for cellular imaging systems--will reach its customers this year. Additional agent-enabled instruments from Danaher businesses that use the platform are planned for 2027, the company said.

"With Microsoft, we are building a common foundation, so our instruments and laboratories work together consistently, as one connected Danaher," said Julie Sawyer Montgomery, Danaher's president and chief executive.

Write to Kelly Cloonan at kelly.cloonan@wsj.com

data.title: Comfort First Heating & Cooling Readies Sanford Drains for Thanksgiving
data.description:
Search Atlas/ Key word(s): Consumer

Comfort First Heating & Cooling Readies Sanford Drains for Thanksgiving

20.11.2026 / 14:15 CET/CEST

The issuer is solely responsible for the content of this announcement.

With Plumbers Bracing for Their Busiest day of the Year, the Sanford Plumbing and HVAC Company Explains how a Full House Strains Kitchen Drains, Toilets and Water Heaters Over the Holiday Weekend

SANFORD, NC - November 20, 2026 (NEWMEDIAWIRE) - Shoppers know the day after Thanksgiving as Black Friday. Plumbers call it Brown Friday. According to plumbing, sewer and drain service provider Roto-Rooter, the day after Thanksgiving sees a 50% spike in service calls, making it the busiest day of the year for the plumbing industry, KTVU FOX 2 reported last year. Roto-Rooter says it also sees a 21% boost in calls from Thursday through Sunday of the holiday weekend.

The cause is a house working harder than usual. Roto-Rooter says pipes and disposals are pushed to their limits with homes full of guests, extra showers and more kitchen use, and that greasy turkey drippings and food scraps add to the clogged drains plumbers see that weekend.

Hot water is part of the same load. Water heater maker Rheem says additional guests and multiple showers in a day increase water heater demand, and that colder inlet water requires a longer heating cycle and higher wattage draw. The company puts the rise in water heater usage at 15-25% in the winter months.

For a Sanford household hosting relatives over the long weekend, all of that lands on one kitchen sink, one water heater and one sewer line in the space of a few days. A disposal that jams on Thursday afternoon, a guest bathroom toilet that will not clear, or showers that run cold by the third guest are the kinds of problems that tend to surface first.

"A kitchen sink that has been draining slowly all fall is usually the one that stops on Thanksgiving," said Adam Hagen, general manager at Comfort First Heating & Cooling. "The holiday does not create the problem so much as find it. Keeping grease and starchy scraps out of the drain, spacing out showers, and paying attention when more than one fixture gurgles at the same time will prevent most of the calls that come in that weekend."

Comfort First Heating & Cooling, founded in 2010, is a full-service HVAC, plumbing and generator company serving Sanford and the wider Triangle area.

  • Pour cooled grease and turkey drippings into a can or jar and throw it away; fats solidify in pipes and choke them.
  • Keep stringy, fibrous or starchy waste such as poultry skin, celery, potato peels and rice out of the garbage disposal, and run the disposal with water while feeding it scraps.
  • Put a plunger and a small wastebasket in each guest bathroom, and ask guests not to flush wet wipes, even ones labelled flushable.
  • Stagger showers and laundry loads across the day so the water heater has time to recover between uses.
  • Listen for a water heater that rumbles or pops, or hot water that runs out sooner than usual, and have it checked before guests arrive.
  • If two or more drains back up or gurgle at the same time, stop running water and call a plumber, since the main sewer line may be the cause.

Sanford homeowners can learn more about plumbing from Comfort First Heating & Cooling online or call (919) 295-3421.

About Comfort First Heating & Cooling

Comfort First Heating & Cooling, founded in 2010, is a North Carolina home-services company offering heating, cooling, plumbing, indoor air quality and generator services. It serves the Triangle, Triad, Charlotte, Jacksonville and Outer Banks areas, including Sanford. Service availability varies by region. More information is available at yourcomfortfirst.com.

Horizon Industrial Parks (Horizon) is India’s largest industrial & logistics (I&L) infrastructure developer, owner and operator by total network with 61.3 msf across 46 assets in ten cities.

Backed by Blackstone, which manages over 1.2 billion sf of logistics assets globally, Horizon serves 130 customers across consumption and manufacturing with Fortune 500 companies accounting for 53 per cent of its committed operational network. Over FY26–29E, we expect consolidated EBITDA to expand at a 34 per cent CAGR to ₹12.6 billion led by new area in large-format parks, scale-up of In-City centres, and MTM and contractual escalations on the existing portfolio.

We value Horizon on a DCF basis with a WACC of 12.5 per cent and an exit 18x FY31E run-rate EBITDA of ₹2,390 crore (derived from 62.6 msf of completed area, average rental of ₹39 psf/month, 97 per cent committed occupancy and 84 per cent EBITDA margin). data.title: Zebra Technologies Releases 2025 Sustainability Report, Outlining Steady Progress Toward Key Goals
data.description:
Zebra Technologies Corporation (), a global leader in digitizing and automating workflows to deliver intelligent operations, today announced the availability of its 2025 Sustainability Report. The publication details steady operational progress on environmental, social, and governance activities across three strategic pillars: Climate, Resource Conservation, and People.

On the climate front, Zebra reduced Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by 42% and key Scope 3 emissions by 28% compared to its 2020 baseline. As part of these efforts in 2025, the company’s Tier 1 manufacturing suppliers utilized an average of 90% renewable energy by spend for the manufacture of Zebra’s products.

"Our progress reflects the collective commitment of our employees, suppliers, and partners," said Bill Burns, chief executive officer, Zebra Technologies. "I am excited about what we have accomplished, and we remain focused on the long-term work ahead and our responsibility to the communities we serve."

Zebra’s sustainability efforts and public reporting of data related to GHG emissions, water usage, waste generation, and related commitments helped the company earn a spot on the Newsweek America’s Greenest Companies list for 2027. The company was also recognized as a Sustainalytics Industry ESG Leader in 2026 and achieved EPEAT (Electronic Product Environmental Assessment Tool) certification for all its eligible new products in 2025.

Conserving Resources to Reduce Waste

To further minimize waste, Zebra implemented targeted resource conservation initiatives across its global facilities. In Flowery Branch, Georgia, the company's label manufacturing facility partnered with iSustain Recycling to introduce a waste-to-energy initiative for complex, multi-component label trimmings. By upgrading internal waste collection infrastructure, the facility now diverts 95% of this previously landfilled material, converting it into Alternative Engineered Fuel (AEF) pellets that displace fossil fuels in industrial systems.

Additionally, a rooftop solar panel system was recently added to Zebra’s supplies manufacturing facility in Preston, U.K. This onsite installation is projected to reduce the facility’s Scope 2 location-based emissions from purchased electricity by 30%.

Fostering Culture and Community through People

In 2025, Zebra employees contributed over 30,000 hours of community service through the Zebra Gives volunteer program. This represents a nearly 15% increase compared to 2024.

Zebra also supports communities where its employees work and live through meaningful, localized engagements. Throughout the year, team members worked with strategic charitable partners on key community-focused initiatives, assembling care kits for patients and families facing pediatric health challenges as well as participating in home construction and repair efforts with Habitat for Humanity.

The 2025 Sustainability report is aligned with leading global disclosure frameworks including the Sustainability Accounting Standards Board (SASB) and the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD).

To learn more, view the full report here.

KEY TAKEAWAYS

  • Zebra achieved a 42% reduction in Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions and a 28% reduction in key Scope 3 emissions compared to its 2020 baseline.
  • Tier 1 manufacturing suppliers utilized an average of 90% renewable energy by spend to manufacture Zebra products in 2025.
  • Global employees volunteered over 30,000 hours through the Zebra Gives program, marking nearly a 15% increase compared to 2024.

WHO IS ZEBRA TECHNOLOGIES?

Zebra () provides the foundation for intelligent operations with an award-winning portfolio of connected frontline, asset visibility and automation solutions which empower our customers to deploy AI on the frontline. Organizations globally across retail, manufacturing, transportation, logistics, healthcare, and other industries rely on us to deliver outcomes today while driving innovation for what’s next. Together with our partners, we create new ways of working that improve productivity and empower organizations to be better every day. Learn more at www.zebra.com.

Follow Zebra on our Blog, LinkedIn, Facebook, X, Instagram and YouTube.
